# Large Load Interconnection

> From the DOE §403 ANOPR (Docket RM26-4-000) to FERC’s June 18, 2026 tailored §206 show cause orders

On October 23, 2025, the Department of Energy invoked its rarely used § 403 authority to direct FERC to open a rulemaking on connecting large loads (data centers, AI, advanced manufacturing) to the interstate grid (Docket RM26-4-000), and asked for final action by April 30, 2026.
Rather than run a multi-year rulemaking, FERC answered on June 18, 2026 with six tailored § 206 show cause orders, one to each RTO/ISO. Each makes a threshold finding that the region’s tariff may be unjust and unreasonable for lack of clear, consistent large-load rules, then puts the market on a 30/60-day clock to defend the status quo or file a fix across the same five reform categories.
The through-line is cost causation made visible: the large load that triggers a network upgrade should bear its cost and spare ordinary ratepayers, with new transparency into how those costs are identified and allocated. The same morning, FERC issued Item E-2 (EL25-49-002), the order on rehearing that finalizes the rates and terms for the three new transmission services its PJM co-location proceeding created, the same services the six orders extend to every other region.
Where it stands on October 19, 2026. All six §206 proceedings are in abeyance to November 16 (SPP: November 20), and the respondents have begun saying in writing what they will do on that date: the PJM Transmission Owners and ISO New England have each committed to a §205 filing by November 16, CAISO takes its proposal to its Board on October 28 for the same date, MISO is filing its reforms under §205 in separate dockets, and NYISO's stated target is December. FERC's one ruling on large-load tariff text since June came on October 9, in PJM's own §205 docket: it accepted a 50 MW Large Load definition and a Large Load Registry and rejected the curtail-first Interim Resource Adequacy Service built around them as an intrusion on state retail jurisdiction. PJM's backstop procurement, accepted and suspended on September 29, is headed for a refiling PJM has promised for October 29. PJM governance is at the redline stage after the Members' September 30 vote, with the states opposed and the Board's filing decision unannounced. Each of these threads has its own line under Where things stand, and the Timeline carries every earlier sweep's findings by date.
The Timeline tab holds the dated record: the August 3 and August 9 answer periods, the August 14 abeyance orders, the August 17 partial co-location compliance, the August 21 governance comments and backstop protests, and everything since. Each entry cites the document it was read from.

A static, independent analysis microsite (not affiliated with FERC or DOE). Source of truth: docs/js/data.js. Evidence is kept in three visibly distinct tiers: FERC primary, DOE primary, and secondary analysis.

## Key facts

- Authority: Federal Power Act § 206 · DOE Organization Act § 403
- Items and dockets: Items E-7 to E-12 · Dockets EL26-67-000 to EL26-72-000
- Reporter cites: 195 FERC ¶ 61,211 to 61,216
- Commission: Laura V. Swett (Chairman) · David Rosner · Lindsay S. See · Judy W. Chang · David LaCerte
- Order record as of 2026-06-22; Discourse commentary gathered through 2026-10-20
- RTOs / ISOs: 6, all FERC-jurisdictional grid operators + their TOs
- Reform categories: 5, teed up in each tailored order
- Informational report: 30 days, resource-adequacy plan to serve large loads
- Justify or file: 60 days, defend tariffs or propose §206 revisions; all six now in abeyance to Nov 16
- “Large load”: > 20 MW, DOE threshold (per Order No. 2003)
- Pages reviewed: 3,500+, public comments in the RM26-4 docket

## The six show cause orders (E-7 to E-12)

Each order PDF is committed and served at the page-precise link below; the official FERC source (Cloudflare-gated) is noted after it.

- [E-7 PJM, EL26-67-000, 195 FERC ¶ 61,211, 114 pp](https://pranava0x0.github.io/FERC-Orders-June-2026/orders/e-7-pjm-el26-67-000.pdf): Co-location rules already in place. Region: Mid-Atlantic / 13 states + DC. Official: https://www.ferc.gov/media/e-7-el26-67-000
- [E-8 MISO, EL26-70-000, 195 FERC ¶ 61,212, 115 pp](https://pranava0x0.github.io/FERC-Orders-June-2026/orders/e-8-miso-el26-70-000.pdf): Early-stage large-load rules. Region: 15 states, Midwest + South. Official: https://www.ferc.gov/media/e-8-el26-70-000
- [E-9 SPP, EL26-68-000, 195 FERC ¶ 61,213, 92 pp](https://pranava0x0.github.io/FERC-Orders-June-2026/orders/e-9-spp-el26-68-000.pdf): Most mature: HILL / HILLGA. Region: Central U.S., 14+ states. Official: https://www.ferc.gov/media/e-9-el26-68-000
- [E-10 CAISO, EL26-71-000, 195 FERC ¶ 61,214, 118 pp](https://pranava0x0.github.io/FERC-Orders-June-2026/orders/e-10-caiso-el26-71-000.pdf): No Order No. 888 service. Region: California (+ WEIM footprint). Official: https://www.ferc.gov/media/e-10-el26-71-000
- [E-11 ISO-NE, EL26-72-000, 195 FERC ¶ 61,215, 115 pp](https://pranava0x0.github.io/FERC-Orders-June-2026/orders/e-11-isone-el26-72-000.pdf): Transmission-constrained grid. Region: Six New England states. Official: https://www.ferc.gov/media/e11-el26-72-000
- [E-12 NYISO, EL26-69-000, 195 FERC ¶ 61,216, 119 pp](https://pranava0x0.github.io/FERC-Orders-June-2026/orders/e-12-nyiso-el26-69-000.pdf): Largely outside the tariff today. Region: New York State. Official: https://www.ferc.gov/media/e12-el26-69-000

## The PJM co-location rehearing order the six extend (Item E-2)

- [E-2 PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., EL25-49-002, 195 FERC ¶ 61,209, 278 pp](https://pranava0x0.github.io/FERC-Orders-June-2026/orders/e-2-pjm-el25-49-002.pdf): Order on rehearing, clarification, compliance & paper hearing on the December 18, 2025 PJM Co-Location Order (193 FERC ¶ 61,217), issued June 18, 2026. Finalizes PJM’s co-location services (Interim NITS, FCD, NFCD) — the services the six §206 orders extend. Official: https://www.ferc.gov/media/e-2-el25-49-002

## The five reform categories

- 1. Application & study processes (incl. alternative transmission technologies): Developing efficient transmission-service application and study processes, including consideration of alternative transmission technologies.
- 2. Cost-shifting prevention & transmission-cost transparency: Preventing cost shifting and requiring transparency into transmission costs.
- 3. Co-location arrangements & behind-the-meter (BTM) generation: Accommodating co-location agreements and behind-the-meter generation.
- 4. New transmission services for flexible large loads: Providing new transmission services for flexible large loads.
- 5. Studying generation serving electrically proximate / co-located loads: Developing a process to study generating facilities that serve electrically proximate large loads and co-located loads.

## Parallel proceedings (as of the 2026-10-20 news sweep)

### The six-market §206 clock (`sc6`)
- Venue: FERC Dockets EL26-67-000 to EL26-72-000
- What: Six show cause orders on one 60-day clock. Each RTO or ISO must defend its tariff or file a fix.
- Why it is tracked separately: This is the main proceeding the site tracks. The other lanes run beside it, each on its own clock.
- Status (2026-10-20): All six proceedings remain in abeyance and the clock has not moved since Aug 14: responses are due Nov 16, 2026 and answers Dec 16, except SPP (Nov 20 and Dec 21). Four weeks out, the respondents' plans are now in writing. The PJM Transmission Owners committed on Oct 9 to a §205 filing on or before Nov 16 covering both the show cause order and their co-location compliance obligation; ISO-NE and its transmission owners said the same day they will file under §205 by Nov 16; CAISO's draft final proposal goes to its Board of Governors on Oct 28 for a Nov 16 filing; MISO has been filing its large-load pieces under §205 in separate ER dockets since August, most recently an Oct 2 fast-track study process (ER27-25); NYISO told FERC in June it aims to file by December, after the Nov 16 date. The Commission's only action in the six dockets since August is the Sept 21 set of orders dismissing, as premature, the rehearing and clarification requests in five of them (PJM, NYISO, MISO, CAISO and ISO-NE); all five orders have now been read, and the Oct 8 sweep's count of four was wrong because it missed the ISO-NE order. Outside the six dockets, FERC's Oct 9 order on PJM's own §205 filing accepted a 50 MW Large Load definition and a Large Load Registry while rejecting the curtailment service built around them. The six docket sheets, read row by row through Oct 20, show nothing substantive since Oct 8: a service-list update in all six and one out-of-time intervention in EL26-67. No respondent has filed in its show cause docket.
- Next: 2026-11-16, Show-cause responses due after the 90-day abeyance (SPP: Nov 20)
  - Dec 16, 2026: Answers due 30 days after the rescheduled responses
  - After the response records close: FERC decides whether to accept, modify, or impose a §206 remedy
  - Parallel lane: Rehearing and court-review risk runs alongside implementation

### PJM co-location: EL25-49 (`e2`)
- Venue: FERC Docket EL25-49 (Item E-2, order on rehearing)
- What: The PJM co-location proceeding that created the three new transmission services the six orders extend to every other region.
- Why it is tracked separately: A different docket with its own compliance clock, which has tracked the §206 clock closely: both were reset to Nov 16, 2026 on the same day, by separate FERC actions.
- Status (2026-10-20): Unchanged on the clock: PJM's and the PJM Transmission Owners' full co-location compliance filing is due Nov 16, 2026, the same date as the §206 clock. The transmission owners' Oct 9 consultation notice folds this obligation into the single §205 filing they have committed to make on or before Nov 16. New on the docket: PJM's Oct 15 answer to the Sep 8 limited protests of its Aug 17 partial compliance filing. PJM now suggests FERC defer ruling on the August tariff changes, for which it had asked an Oct 17 effective date, until the November filing completes the record, and it pushes its own Interim NITS timeline out: requests accepted from September 2027, a unified study of large loads and generation in 2028, service from the first quarter of 2029. No Commission order since the Aug 14 extension; the sheet was read through Oct 20.
- Next: 2026-11-16, PJM and PJM TOs full co-location compliance filing
  - Aug 14, 2026: The co-location compliance deadline moves to the same date
  - Aug 17, 2026: PJM files partial co-location compliance anyway, and dates one service to 2028
  - Oct 15, 2026: PJM answers the protests of its co-location compliance filing, and asks FERC to wait for November

### PJM governance: AD26-7 (`gov`)
- Venue: FERC Docket AD26-7-000 (Commission-led technical conference)
- What: A July 23 conference on who runs PJM: board independence, the stakeholder process, and the states’ role.
- Why it is tracked separately: Runs outside the §206 clock. Its September deadlines decide who controls PJM’s follow-through filings.
- Also known as: Also referred to in shorthand as the Swett technical conference, after the chairman who convened it.
- Status (2026-10-20): PJM is drafting the Members' term sheet into tariff language. On Oct 13 it posted Operating Agreement and Tariff redlines implementing the sheet the Members endorsed Sept 30 (§205 rights over the energy-market schedules with a jump-ball rule for competing Member filings, 30 days' notice of market-design filings, a permanent planning committee in the Operating Agreement, an independence clause), and walked stakeholders through them at an Oct 16 page-turn workshop. The redlines are a stakeholder draft, not a filing, and nothing says yet whether the Board will file the Members' package, its own, or neither. The record so far: FERC's Dispute Resolution Service opened confidential talks on Sept 1; on Sept 30 a special Members Committee approved the Members' sheet by the required sector-weighted two-thirds vote, ahead of PJM's and the Consumer Advocates' versions, neither of which won a majority; PJM told FERC so on Oct 1 and noted that the Organization of PJM States and the PJM Governors' Collaborative do not find the result satisfactory. The states had written to the Board on Sept 29 that if the Members' sheet passed they would “forcefully oppose it before the Commission and beyond.” FERC has not acted on the vote, its Oct 15 open meeting carried no governance item, and the AD26-7 docket sheet, read through Oct 20, has nothing new since Oct 8.
- Next: 2026-10-28, Members Committee meets; the Board's decision on what to file at FERC is still unannounced
  - Sep 1, 2026: FERC's mediators open confidential talks on PJM governance
  - Sep 30, 2026: PJM's Members vote through their own governance term sheet, and the states object
  - Oct 16, 2026: PJM walks members through the tariff redlines for the Members' governance sheet

### The RM26-4 record (`rm264`)
- Venue: FERC Docket RM26-4-000 (the DOE §403 rulemaking)
- What: The rulemaking DOE’s §403 directive opened, and the 3,500-plus pages of comment the orders were built on.
- Why it is tracked separately: Still open. Everything the six orders left unaddressed stays live here, which is what the record-to-rule crosswalk tracks.
- Status (2026-10-19): Open with no dated next step, and nothing new on it since the June 18 orders. FERC answered the directive with the six §206 orders rather than a rule, and its Oct 15 open meeting agenda carried no RM26-4 item. The record's substance now moves through the regional §205 filings the orders invited; the crosswalk on the Comments tab tracks which of the record's issues each order reached.
- Next: No dated step on the record
  - Oct 23, 2025: DOE issues a § 403 directive + enclosed ANOPR
  - Oct 23, 2025: Fourteen ANOPR principles define the reform menu
  - Late 2025 to Jan 2026: FERC opens RM26-4-000, takes comment, extends the period

### Market context (`context`)
- Venue: not a docket
- What: Auction results and market events that set the stakes for the filings, from outside any of the dockets.
- Why it is tracked separately: Mostly auction results and market events, kept in their own lane so the rail never reads an auction result as a docket event. PJM's backstop procurement (ER26-3380 and EL26-108) sits here too: it is a PJM market mechanism, not part of the large-load show cause clock, and its events name their docket.
- Status (2026-10-20): Two PJM §205 filings, two partial rejections in eleven days. On Oct 9 FERC accepted PJM's 50 MW Large Load definition and Large Load Registry (ER26-3515, 197 FERC ¶ 61,019), effective Oct 12 with a compliance filing due within 30 days, and rejected the rest of the Aug 13 package: the Interim Resource Adequacy Service that would have let new large loads connect without matching capacity in exchange for being curtailed first, the requirement that load-serving entities bring new capacity for them, the Bring Your Own New Capacity rules, and the exclusion of those loads from the capacity-auction demand curve. FERC found the curtailment service places obligations on retail customers, dictates which retail customers are curtailed and sets a retail rate, all of it state territory, and found the rest of the package inextricably linked to it. Commissioner Rosner concurred alone. No one has asked for rehearing of that order as of Oct 20; requests are due Nov 9. On the backstop (ER26-3380, suspended Sept 29 to Feb 28, 2027), PJM moved on Oct 12 (docketed Oct 13) to hold the paper hearing in abeyance and told FERC it will file a new §205 proposal by Oct 29 on cost allocation, transmission owner exit responsibilities and load-serving-entity collateral; FERC set answers to the motion due Oct 21. PJM's deck for its Oct 22 member consultation adds dropping the municipal and cooperative opt-out FERC called unduly discriminatory, and proposes a March 1 to March 22, 2027 bid window. The EL26-108 refund effective date is Oct 6, 2026, the Federal Register publication date. DOE's Oct 7 statement of position urged the Oct 29 refiling.
- Next: 2026-10-29, PJM's stated date for the new backstop §205 filing, and the end of FERC's 30-day window for holding the paper hearing in abeyance
  - Oct 21, 2026: Answers due on PJM's backstop abeyance motion
  - Oct 22, 2026: PJM consults its Members Committee on the backstop refiling
  - Oct 29, 2026: PJM's date for the new backstop §205 filing, and the end of FERC's 30-day window

## Observed filings (checked 2026-10-20)

- Observed filings only. An empty cell means our checks found nothing, which is not proof nothing was filed. Every report and abeyance cell below is confirmed against its own eLibrary accession. Every abeyance motion was GRANTED on Aug 14, 2026, so the show-cause column is upcoming again, now against Nov 16 (Nov 20 for SPP) rather than Aug 17; each cell's gist carries the granting order's accession and reporter citation. A show-cause cell marked Signaled rests on the respondent's own written statement of what it will file (its source is cited in the cell), not on anything observed on the docket. The six sheets were read through Oct 20 and no respondent had filed a show cause response or a §205 proposal in its docket.
- Status vocabulary: `filed-verified` (eLibrary accession seen) · `filed-reported` (press or operator channel only) · `signaled` (announced intent). An absent row means our checks observed nothing, which is not proof nothing was filed.
- PJM (EL26-67-000), showcause, signaled, 2026-10-09: The PJM Transmission Owners' Oct 9 consultation notice commits them to a §205 filing on or before Nov 16 covering the show cause order and their EL25-49 compliance obligation. PJM itself told FERC in its abeyance motion to expect its §205 filing in early-to-mid November, with an advisory Members Committee vote Oct 28. Neither filing has been observed.
- ISO-NE (EL26-72-000), showcause, signaled, 2026-10-09: ISO-NE's Oct 9 proposal summary: the ISO and the Participating Transmission Owners Administrative Committee will develop a §205 filing to be submitted by Nov 16, 2026. Not yet observed on the docket.
- MISO (EL26-70-000), showcause, signaled, 2026-10-02: MISO is filing its large-load reforms under §205 in separate ER dockets rather than in EL26-70: a zero-injection generator interconnection agreement in August and, on Oct 2, a Large Load Addition Resource Study in Docket ER27-25-000 (accession 20261002-5074), with a requested effective date of Dec 2, 2026. Whether MISO also files or responds in EL26-70 by Nov 16 is unknown.
- NYISO (EL26-69-000), showcause, signaled, 2026-06-18: NYISO's own target, as recorded in its show cause order, is to file corresponding tariff revisions by December 2026, after the Nov 16 reset date. Nothing later from NYISO was found this sweep.

- ISO-NE (EL26-72-000), report, filed-verified, 2026-07-20: Informational filing on regional resource adequacy. Outlines requiring new large loads to bring incremental new generation, and not procuring capacity for them through the regional capacity market. Accession: 20260720-5216.
- PJM (EL26-67-000), abeyance, filed-verified, 2026-07-28: PJM Interconnection moves to hold the proceeding in abeyance with a shortened answer period; the Indicated PJM Transmission Owners file a parallel motion the same day. Filed five days ahead of the deadline. FERC sets an answer period Jul 30 (20260730-3026); Constellation and the PJM Industrial Customer Coalition answer in support Aug 3. Granted Aug 14 (letter order 20260814-3059, 196 FERC ¶ 61,129), together with the Indicated PJM TOs' and Silver Run Electric's motions; responses reset to Nov 16, 2026. Accession: 20260728-5084.

Granted Aug 14 (letter order 20260814-3060, 196 FERC ¶ 61,128) for the 95 days the movants asked for rather than 90; responses reset to Nov 20, 2026, the latest of the six. Accession: 20260803-5209.

All three motions granted Aug 14 (letter order 20260814-3068, 196 FERC ¶ 61,130); responses reset to Nov 16, 2026. Accession: 20260803-5229.
- MISO (EL26-70-000), abeyance, filed-verified, 2026-08-03: Joint motion of MISO and the MISO Transmission Owners to hold the proceeding in abeyance. Granted Aug 14 (letter order 20260814-3058, 196 FERC ¶ 61,133) over American Municipal Power's opposition, without AMP's proposed 20-day condition but with an express reminder that any preliminary finding the §205 filings leave unaddressed returns to the show cause proceeding; responses reset to Nov 16, 2026. Accession: 20260803-5249.
- CAISO (EL26-71-000), abeyance, filed-verified, 2026-08-03: CAISO moves for abeyance; a coalition of California transmission owners (SCE, SDG&E, PG&E and others) files a separate joint abeyance request the same day. The “Six Cities” (Anaheim, Azusa, Banning, Colton, Pasadena, Riverside) file a conditional abeyance motion, having already moved Jul 31 to rescind the order outright; the Western Area Power Administration separately moves to rescind as applied to itself. Granted Aug 14 by full order (20260814-3061, 196 FERC ¶ 61,131), which also granted the Six Cities' and WAPA's motions to rescind the order as against them under FPA §201(f) and amended the caption; responses reset to Nov 16, 2026. Accession: 20260803-5206.
- ISO-NE (EL26-72-000), abeyance, filed-verified, 2026-08-03: Joint motion of ISO New England and the Participating Transmission Owners Administrative Committee to hold the proceeding in abeyance, following through on the intent signaled Jun 29. Granted Aug 14 (letter order 20260814-3056, 196 FERC ¶ 61,132); responses reset to Nov 16, 2026. Accession: 20260803-5083.
- CAISO (EL26-71-000), showcause, filed-verified, 2026-08-12: Morongo Transmission LLC, a CAISO participating transmission owner owned by the Morongo Band of Mission Indians, answers that no amendment to its tariff is required because it is a non-load-serving transmission owner with no end-use customers, while stating it will keep participating in the proceeding. Filed two days before the abeyance and the only substantive answer to any of the six show cause orders observed to date. Accession: 20260812-5158.

## Commentary themes (secondary, in three dated waves)

- [wave 1, reaction to the June 18 orders, captured 2026-06-29] Cost responsibility is the center of gravity: Across the post-order discussion, the basic question is not whether large loads should connect faster; it is whether the tariff makes the beneficiary carry the cost and risk of the upgrade.
  - "There’s no real quarantining of the cost caused by data centers to those data centers" Source: https://insideclimatenews.org/news/18062026/federal-energy-regulatory-commission-data-center-orders/
  - "those loads bear the costs incurred to serve them" Source: https://www.linkedin.com/posts/jeffdennis77_ecaferclargeloadinterconnectionstatementpdf-activity-7473477334738599936-NWa-
  - "increasing scrutiny on who pays for transmission to connect data centers" Source: https://x.com/aniruddh_mohan/status/2069973894237184457
  - "President Trump's Ratepayer Protection Pledge" Source: https://www.energy.gov/articles/department-energy-applauds-fercs-action-large-load-interconnection-reform
- [wave 1, reaction to the June 18 orders, captured 2026-06-29] The regional route is both substance and litigation strategy: The six-order structure is being read as a deliberate alternative to one national template: faster than a rulemaking, more tailored to each market, and easier to defend on the record.
  - "far more substantively ambitious than the ANOPR" Source: https://www.utilitydive.com/news/ferc-doe-data-center-interconnection/823360/
  - "six regional answers to the same question, decided on six different timelines" Source: https://www.utilitydive.com/news/ferc-doe-data-center-interconnection/823360/
  - "a much more robust and detailed administrative record" Source: https://news.bloomberglaw.com/environment-and-energy/energy-regulator-staves-off-critique-in-new-data-center-orders
  - "reduces future litigation entry points" Source: https://news.bloomberglaw.com/environment-and-energy/energy-regulator-staves-off-critique-in-new-data-center-orders
- [wave 1, reaction to the June 18 orders, captured 2026-06-29] Speed now depends on provable flexibility: The strongest pro-speed argument treats data centers as controllable loads, but the quotes also show the hard edge: flexibility has to be operational, measurable, and worth something in the tariff.
  - "emergency data-center load reduction ripe for deeper industry analysis" Source: https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/demand-hereare-we-ready-build-briggs-white-cixae
  - "flexible AI data centers can adjust demand dynamically and act as grid assets, not only as fixed loads" Source: https://www.latitudemedia.com/news/catalyst-the-rise-of-flexible-data-centers/
  - "asset-backed flexible data centers can operate as grid assets" Source: https://www.volts.wtf/p/can-data-centers-be-good-grid-citizens
  - "paying other customers to shift load can be faster and more cost effective than curtailing expensive data-center chips" Source: https://www.eenews.net/articles/how-big-tech-learned-to-speak-ferc/
- [wave 1, reaction to the June 18 orders, captured 2026-06-29] Reliability and security remain live objections: The order is not landing as a pure acceleration story. Consumer and security voices are treating faster interconnection as acceptable only if modeling, operating standards, and stability protections keep up.
  - "security gaps remain" Source: https://x.com/BenSchifman/article/2067679572431138993
  - "data centers need any more help with interconnection to the grid" Source: https://x.com/Ben_Inskeep/status/2068025625860841880
  - "standards and rules in place that protect ratepayers from any negative stability, reliability and resiliency impacts" Source: https://x.com/Ben_Inskeep/status/2068025625860841880
- [wave 1, reaction to the June 18 orders, captured 2026-06-29] The physical buildout is bigger than the FERC clock: The discourse keeps returning to the same physical constraint: the orders can compress process, but turbines, transformers, generation, local consent, and deliverable capacity still decide which projects energize.
  - "power conversations for individual data centers have moved from megawatts to gigawatts" Source: https://cleanpower.org/blog/american-energy-american-ai-powering-a-secure-future/
  - "gas-turbine, transformer and interconnection lead times" Source: https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/demand-hereare-we-ready-build-briggs-white-cixae
  - "power constraints and political resistance" Source: https://www.shanumathew.com/writing/data-centers-focus-on-energized-gw
  - "developers are pairing data-center growth with behind-the-meter generation and siting near stranded or underused power" Source: https://www.argusmedia.com/en/news-and-insights/latest-market-news/2804882-us-grid-overhaul-urgently-needed-to-meet-ai-load-ferc
- [wave 1, reaction to the June 18 orders, captured 2026-06-29] The organized-market focus leaves a Southeast gap: The order covers the six RTO/ISO markets, while several reactions flag the regions outside that structure as exactly where transmission planning and interconnection practice may be weakest.
  - "non-RTO areas, which typically suffer from the worst transmission and interconnection practices" Source: https://www.utilitydive.com/news/ferc-doe-data-center-interconnection/823360/
  - "The Southeast needs a modern transmission system" Source: https://ceba.org/southeast-energy-opportunities-require-a-bigger-better-faster-grid-business-leaders-call-for-regional-transmission-planning/
  - "we risk higher energy prices, power shortages, and lost economic opportunities" Source: https://ceba.org/southeast-energy-opportunities-require-a-bigger-better-faster-grid-business-leaders-call-for-regional-transmission-planning/
- [wave 1, reaction to the June 18 orders, captured 2026-10-20] The state line: FERC claims no new retail reach: On the day of the orders the state regulators' association reserved judgment on substance but welcomed the commissioners' nod to state authority. A law-firm read of the orders put the same point plainly: FERC stayed inside its existing jurisdiction and left retail questions with the states. By July, state consumer advocates were arguing that this was the problem; their case is in the summer lane.
  - "We appreciate the Commissioners’ comments at today’s meeting recognizing the critical role of states and state regulators given the jurisdictional division of duties under the Federal Power Act." Source: https://pubs.naruc.org/pub/A037DD09-A293-2927-B215-CD0CBE9FC0A4
  - "States remain committed to ensuring the appropriate allocation of costs across all customer classes and working constructively with our federal colleagues to that end." Source: https://pubs.naruc.org/pub/A037DD09-A293-2927-B215-CD0CBE9FC0A4
  - "Importantly, FERC did not assert any new or expanded jurisdiction over retail load or co-located load in a broad or preemptive sense." Source: https://www.hklaw.com/en/insights/publications/2026/06/ferc-advances-new-oversight-framework-for-large-loads
- [wave 2, the filings and the governance fight, captured 2026-07-28] PJM’s own legitimacy becomes the story: The July 23 technical conference put PJM’s decision-making machinery on the record, and on a September clock. The same commission running the §206 filings is now asking who gets to decide what PJM files, which makes this lane a precondition for the other one rather than a sideshow.
  - "PJM is facing a grave legitimacy crisis" Source: https://www.utilitydive.com/news/ferc-pjm-governance-reforms-data-centers-capacity-market/826140/
  - "Some transmission owners are openly discussing leaving the RTO altogether" Source: https://www.utilitydive.com/news/ferc-pjm-governance-reforms-data-centers-capacity-market/826140/
  - "This is a cultural quagmire" Source: https://www.utilitydive.com/news/ferc-pjm-governance-reforms-data-centers-capacity-market/826140/
- [wave 2, the filings and the governance fight, captured 2026-07-28] Regional divergence: the tailoring thesis meets the record: The first observed answer to the 30-day reports points somewhere different from PJM’s expedited-new-entry posture. ISO-NE looks to new generation and away from its capacity market. That is the regional variation the six tailored orders were built to permit, showing up as substance rather than as a gap.
  - "requiring new large loads to bring incremental new generation" Source: https://isonewswire.com/2026/07/21/update-on-iso-ne-compliance-with-ferc-large-and-co-located-loads-order/
  - "not procuring capacity through the regional capacity market to serve these large loads" Source: https://isonewswire.com/2026/07/21/update-on-iso-ne-compliance-with-ferc-large-and-co-located-loads-order/
  - "intend to request a 90-day abeyance" Source: https://isonewswire.com/2026/06/29/iso-ne-provides-update-on-compliance-with-ferc-large-loads-order/
- [wave 2, the filings and the governance fight, captured 2026-07-28] Capacity scarcity is the arithmetic behind the argument: PJM’s 2028/2029 auction cleared at its cap for the third year running and still landed short of the reserve-margin target. Every claim about who should pay for new load is being made against that number.
  - "The price came in at the FERC-approved cap of $325/MW-day" Source: https://www.pjm.com/-/media/DotCom/about-pjm/newsroom/2026-releases/20260714-pjm-capacity-auction-procures-138318-mw-generation-resources.pdf
  - "short of PJM’s 20% installed reserve margin target by 6,831 MW" Source: https://www.pjm.com/-/media/DotCom/about-pjm/newsroom/2026-releases/20260714-pjm-capacity-auction-procures-138318-mw-generation-resources.pdf
- [wave 2, the filings and the governance fight, captured 2026-10-20] State advocates: transparency is not a remedy: On July 17 Maryland's People's Counsel, joined by the Ohio, Delaware and Illinois advocates, asked FERC to rehear the PJM order, and Pennsylvania's advocate filed separately. Their argument is that the order makes data-center transmission costs visible to states but leaves PJM's cost allocation in place, and states cannot move costs between transmission customers. Ari Peskoe of Harvard's Electricity Law Initiative sided with them. FERC dismissed every request on Sept 21 because the order had not decided anything yet.
  - "The order erroneously assumes State regulators have authority that they do not clearly have." Source: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MDOPC/bulletins/420fd48
  - "Each network upgrade added to a transmission owner’s revenue requirement while these questions remain open embeds another cost shift" Source: https://www.utilitydive.com/news/ferc-data-center-pjm-transmission-costs/825760/
  - "Unjust and unreasonable wholesale transmission cost shifts from large loads in PJM can manifest through unjust and unreasonable cost allocation of both [Regional Transmission Expansion Plan] projects and supplemental projects" Source: https://www.utilitydive.com/news/ferc-data-center-pjm-transmission-costs/825760/
  - "That move violates the law. PJM's Tariff guarantees cost shifts due to transmission for data centers. Only FERC can fix that. And it must." Source: https://x.com/AriPeskoe/status/2079226485626249625
  - "It did not order the utilities to charge those upgrade costs to data centers. They are still spread to everyone." Source: https://x.com/AriPeskoe/status/2080348438655295648
  - "We therefore dismiss the requests for rehearing, which concern a Commission action that is not final and that will be succeeded by further Commission action." Source: https://www.pjm.com/-/media/DotCom/documents/ferc/orders/2026/20260921-el26-67-001.pdf
- [wave 3, October: the retail line, and the refilings, captured 2026-10-20] FERC draws the retail line under PJM's curtail-first service: The Oct 9 order on ER26-3515 is the first FERC ruling on large-load tariff text since June 18, and the ground it chose was jurisdiction rather than policy. The interim service fell because it reached retail customers; the definition and the registry survived because they do not. Analysts read the result as support for existing generators, and PJM's own reaction kept to cost causation.
  - "several provisions of the proposed Tariff appear to place obligations directly on Eligible New Large Loads, which are, for the most part, retail customers" Source: https://www.pjm.com/pjmfiles/directory/etariff/FercOrders/9207/20261009-er26-3515-000.pdf
  - "the proposed compensation framework appears to establish a retail rate" Source: https://www.pjm.com/pjmfiles/directory/etariff/FercOrders/9207/20261009-er26-3515-000.pdf
  - "we strongly encourage states to continue their important work on this issue" Source: https://www.pjm.com/pjmfiles/directory/etariff/FercOrders/9207/20261009-er26-3515-000.pdf
  - "honoring the concept that existing electricity customers should not be unfairly burdened by new, energy intensive customers" Source: https://www.utilitydive.com/news/ferc-pjm-large-load-interconnection-iras-byonc/832716/
  - "the latest development is positive for existing generation/IPPs" Source: https://www.utilitydive.com/news/ferc-pjm-large-load-interconnection-iras-byonc/832716/
- [wave 3, October: the retail line, and the refilings, captured 2026-10-20] Rosner: curtail data centers last, and only after demand response: The one separate statement on the Oct 9 order. Commissioner Rosner agreed with rejecting the package and wrote to say what a refiled version would have to justify: forcing new large loads off the system before customers who volunteered for demand response, and excluding those loads from the capacity-market demand curve while the region sheds them involuntarily.
  - "That’s not only economically inefficient, but also likely to prevent supply and demand from coming back into balance." Source: https://www.pjm.com/pjmfiles/directory/etariff/FercOrders/9207/20261009-er26-3515-000.pdf
  - "We need state regulators to establish clear rules for which customers should be curtailed first when circumstances require it." Source: https://www.pjm.com/pjmfiles/directory/etariff/FercOrders/9207/20261009-er26-3515-000.pdf
  - "such measures should only be taken when necessary to keep the system reliable, after voluntary demand response resources have been exhausted" Source: https://www.pjm.com/pjmfiles/directory/etariff/FercOrders/9207/20261009-er26-3515-000.pdf
  - "in an emergency, data centers not serving critical functions should be shut off before ordinary customers" Source: https://www.pjm.com/pjmfiles/directory/etariff/FercOrders/9207/20261009-er26-3515-000.pdf
- [wave 3, October: the retail line, and the refilings, captured 2026-10-20] PJM answers two setbacks with refilings, not rehearing: After the Sept 29 backstop order and the Oct 9 large-load order, PJM's public posture is the same both times: review, then refile fast. Its Oct 22 consultation deck names Oct 29 for the new backstop filing and lists the fixes, including dropping the municipal and cooperative opt-out FERC called unduly discriminatory.
  - "PJM is reviewing the order and intends to work quickly to address the Commission’s remaining concerns." Source: https://insidelines.pjm.com/ferc-accepts-pjm-reliability-backstop-proposal/
  - "PJM submitted a motion for abeyance of the paper hearing on October 12 and notified FERC that it plans to submit a new 205 filing to FERC on October 29th" Source: https://www.pjm.com/-/media/DotCom/committees-groups/committees/mc/2026/20261022-special/item-01---1-tariff-section-92b-stakeholder-consultation-of-upcoming-205-filing-on-reliability-backstop-procurement---presentation.pdf
  - "Remove the opt out for muni/co-ops." Source: https://www.pjm.com/-/media/DotCom/committees-groups/committees/mc/2026/20261022-special/item-01---1-tariff-section-92b-stakeholder-consultation-of-upcoming-205-filing-on-reliability-backstop-procurement---presentation.pdf
- [wave 3, October: the retail line, and the refilings, captured 2026-10-20] Nov 16 is turning into a §205 date: Four weeks before the reset deadline, the respondents are saying in their own documents that they will file tariff changes rather than defend the status quo: the PJM transmission owners and ISO-NE in writing on Oct 9, MISO by filing pieces as it goes, PJM with a ride-through standard it says it will file in November.
  - "The PJM Transmission Owners have committed to submit their proposed revisions to address the concerns identified by the June 18, 2026 order issued in Docket No. EL26-67-000" Source: https://www.pjm.com/-/media/DotCom/committees-groups/committees/mc/2026/20261028/20261028-notice-of-pjm-transmission-owners-consultation-with-the-members-committee---informational-posting-only.pdf
  - "The ISO and the Participating Transmission Owners Administrative Committee (PTO AC) were granted an abeyance and will develop a Section 205 filing to be submitted by November 16, 2026." Source: https://www.iso-ne.com/static-assets/documents/100040/large_loads_integration_proposal_information_summary_10.09.26.pdf
  - "LARS provides MISO with a targeted tool to address the intersection of significant large load additions," Source: https://www.utilitydive.com/news/miso-large-load-generation-study-lars-ferc/832114/
  - "This type of operation is unsustainable and needs to be addressed," Source: https://insidelines.pjm.com/reliability-standards-to-manage-large-load-disconnection-events-proposed-by-pjm/
- [wave 3, October: the retail line, and the refilings, captured 2026-10-20] The backstop bill: who pays for capacity bought for new load: PJM's backstop buys capacity for a shortfall that large loads are driving, so the argument is over who carries the cost. Before FERC ruled, NRDC's Claire Lang-Ree read the proposal as PJM refusing to keep buying power for data centers, and Maryland People's Counsel David Lapp warned that households would pay if the forecast load never arrived. Two concurrences on the Sept 29 order answered: Chairman Swett faulted a filing made on the last possible day, and Commissioner See wrote that existing customers should not carry costs new demand causes. Ari Peskoe called FERC's cost-allocation objection surprising; DOE backed the order on Oct 9.
  - "PJM is saying very clearly to the data centers, 'We will no longer buy power on your behalf,'" Source: https://www.wypr.org/wypr-news/2026-08-26/pjm-looks-to-implement-key-data-center-regulations-maryland-energy-stakeholders-have-mixed-feelings
  - "If the data centers don't show up in those zones, then it'll be the existing customers, ordinary households included, that will pay those costs." Source: https://www.wypr.org/wypr-news/2026-08-26/pjm-looks-to-implement-key-data-center-regulations-maryland-energy-stakeholders-have-mixed-feelings
  - "This Commission will not be forced into accepting a deeply flawed, eleventh-hour procurement mechanism with billion-dollar implications for consumers." Source: https://www.pjm.com/pjmfiles/directory/etariff/FercOrders/9154/20260929-er26-3380-000.pdf
  - "Existing customers should not be left paying costs attributable to new demand." Source: https://www.pjm.com/pjmfiles/directory/etariff/FercOrders/9154/20260929-er26-3380-000.pdf
  - "Surprising! FERC has issues with the cost allocation framework that determined who pays for this data center capacity auction." Source: https://x.com/AriPeskoe/status/2105250742596784234
  - "the Energy Department supports having large electricity users pay for reliable new power generation" Source: https://www.energy.gov/articles/energy-department-supports-fercs-call-pjm-protect-ratepayers-and-build-more-reliable-power
- [wave 3, October: the retail line, and the refilings, captured 2026-10-20] After Oct 9, the states hold the pen on curtailment: FERC rejected PJM's curtail-first service as a reach into retail jurisdiction, and the reactions agree on the consequence: the next move belongs to the states. Jeff Dennis read the order as more pressure on them. Mary Yang, a former PJM regulatory counsel now at 804 Advisory, said it slows bring-your-own-capacity deals. NRDC wants PJM to refile with a bring-your-own-supply rule. And in a Duke Energy Carolinas order the same day, outside the RTOs, Commissioner Rosner wrote that FERC may have to widen the show cause orders' cost-recovery framework if state action falls short.
  - "In doing so, it appears to be putting more pressure on states to find answers." Source: https://x.com/EnergyLawJeff/status/2109669734568304766
  - "It does slow down the development of these more innovative bilateral mechanisms to solve some of these problems" Source: https://www.latitudemedia.com/news/ferc-rejected-pjms-data-center-curtailment-plan-whats-next-for-byoc/
  - "At a minimum, PJM's rules must require data centers to bring their own supply, and not allow them to raise electricity costs or cause blackouts" Source: https://www.bisnow.com/news/national/data-center-power/federal-regulators-reject-power-cuts-to-data-centers-that-dont-bring-their-own
  - "To the extent state regulatory actions are not sufficient to protect consumers, the Commission has an obligation to seriously consider expanding the cost recovery framework it established in the Large Load Show Cause Orders" Source: https://elibrary.ferc.gov/eLibrary/search

## The RM26-4 public comments (corpus)

- 273 public comments (of 423 total eLibrary filings) on the DOE ANOPR (Docket RM26-4-000) were scraped from FERC eLibrary. Each text-extracted comment carries a quote-centric, auditable summary built the PNNL "CommentNEPA" way: verbatim quotes pulled from the filing, binned to the five reform principles / eight ANOPR questions / six regions (plus emergent topics), each bin with the filer's stance. AI-generated and provisional (not yet human-verified).
- Per-comment summaries: `sources/comments/summaries-v2/<accession>.json`. Compiled for the site: `docs/js/comments-data.js` (`window.FERC_COMMENTS`). Method + schema: `sources/comments/summarization-spec.md`. Explore on the Comments tab (a stance map + per-comment audited analysis).
